props.text:
Everyone is matched.
So why can this pairing
still fall apart?

beats.narration_text: Start with A paired to X and B paired to Y. Every seat is filled, yet A prefers Y, and Y prefers A. That unmatched pair would defect together, so complete does not mean stable.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Start with A paired to X and B paired to Y. Every seat is filled, yet A prefers Y, and Y prefers A. That unmatched pair would defect together, so complete does not mean stable.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 1 · Complete matching animates; explicit A–Y blocking pair appears with preference ranks.

beats.narration_text: Change just Y’s ranking so Y prefers B. The same drawn matching now has no mutual defection between A and Y. Stability depends on both preference lists, not on crossed or uncrossed lines.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Change just Y's ranking so Y prefers B. The same drawn matching now has no mutual defection between A and Y. Stability depends on both preference lists, not on crossed or uncrossed lines.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 2 · Same subject persists while Y's ranking transforms and blocking status flips explicitly.

beats.narration_text: Now three students propose. S one and S three both choose C one first. C one currently holds S one. Before the next step, predict whether that engagement is permanent.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Now three students propose. S one and S three both choose C one first. C one currently holds S one. Before the next step, predict whether that engagement is permanent.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PREDICT · Live proposal state holds; question writes on in hai-simple treatment.

beats.narration_text: It is only tentative. C one compares the new proposal, keeps S one, and rejects S three. S three moves down exactly one place to C three; rejected choices never return.
beats.tts_normalized_text: It is only tentative. C one compares the new proposal, keeps S one, and rejects S three. S three moves down exactly one place to C three; rejected choices never return.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRACE 1 / TRANSFORM · Proposals, rejection, and pointer movement animate on split stage.

beats.narration_text: Run a second preference profile. C one first holds S one, then trades upward to S two. S one becomes free and proposes next to C two. Every rejection advances one pointer.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Run a second preference profile. C one first holds S one, then trades upward to S two. S one becomes free and proposes next to C two. Every rejection advances one pointer.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE INSTANCE 3 / TRACE 2 · Receiver trade-up and displaced proposer pointer run completely.

beats.narration_text: Those traces reveal the license: progress is monotone. Proposers move only downward through finite lists; receivers keep only their best offer so far. No decision moves backward.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Those traces reveal the license: progress is monotone. Proposers move only downward through finite lists; receivers keep only their best offer so far. No decision moves backward.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE ABSTRACTION · Characteristics named only after traces; pointers and receiver ranks keep operating on split stage.

beats.narration_text: Suppose the final matching had a blocking pair, A and Y. A must have proposed to Y before reaching a worse partner. Y rejected A only for someone Y preferred, and never traded downward. So Y cannot prefer A at the end—a contradiction.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Suppose the final matching had a blocking pair, A and Y. A must have proposed to Y before reaching a worse partner. Y rejected A only for someone Y preferred, and never traded downward. So Y cannot prefer A at the end, a contradiction.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE TRANSFORM / PROOF · Blocking-pair hypothesis rewinds to proposal, then receiver rank moves upward and invalidates it.

beats.narration_text: Return to the opening mismatch. Deferred acceptance cannot leave A and Y both wanting to defect. If A prefers Y, Y must already hold someone Y ranks above A. The hidden blocking pair is gone.
beats.tts_normalized_text: Return to the opening mismatch. Deferred acceptance cannot leave A and Y both wanting to defect. If A prefers Y, Y must already hold someone Y ranks above A. The hidden blocking pair is gone.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE PAYOFF · Same hook objects return and the A–Y candidate pair is rejected by explicit ranks.

beats.narration_text: The verdict: engagements are deferred, not promises. One side moves down; the other trades up. Those two monotone directions force termination and rule out every blocking pair.
beats.tts_normalized_text: The verdict: engagements are deferred, not promises. One side moves down; the other trades up. Those two monotone directions force termination and rule out every blocking pair.
beats.new_visual_element: ROLE VERDICT · ClaudeVerdictArtifact recap from the film's own proposals and ranks.

artifactLines: Complete ≠ stable: A and Y can form a blocking pair
Proposers move down finite preference lists
Receivers trade up and never trade down
Therefore every rejection is permanent—and no blocking pair survives
